searchText: Is there a checklist of things or bugs to get fixed the devs want to accomplish before scheduling a date for the Sepolia testnet merge? Just curious how the various teams decide when everything is ready. Or maybe an alternative way to ask this is-is there an outstanding issue looking to be fixed before the next testnet merge is scheduled? Hi all! when and where are the merge meeting w core devs - ty! Youtube “ethereum foundation” https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/988633522736594974 <@301186049323958275> you want the keys to be as small as possible while still being secure for performance reasons I thought there was some special thing that made 224 significantly easier than 225 bits. Am I mistaken? Like there was some threshold across which stuff suddenly got much harder. ah, I am not aware of that generally they are less than 256 bits as ethereum uses that, and you want to be able to store the key on less than 256. Then you want to find some number that is easy to do calculations with the ones that are easier to do calculations are close to some power of two, so maybe there are more primes near power of twos with 224 bits than 225? You mean `224 bits` is `2^6 * 7`, while `225` bits doesn't have any factors of `2`? yeah <@301186049323958275> I'm not working on the merge directly, so <#892088344438255616> is read-only for me. In regards to https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/988633836193742888 I think less than 256 bits would generally be better for proving time: As an analogy, in a 64 bit architecture, the word size is 64 bits, so if you have a datatype which requires more than 64 bits to encode its information, then you'd need multiple words. Like a u65 would need 2 64 bit words. Also adding a u65 would have more complexity to it than adding a u64 or something than is less than 64 bits. For zk proofs, we usually have a word size that is just less than 256 bits, so to encode a 256 bit number we would also need 2 words/field elements. If its not used too often, it might be okay I think, I'd need to check the exact system/usage to determine whether the blowup may be significant. Reasons I would not go for 234 bits would be because it may reduce the security of the system as a whole, If we are using 234 bits or even less in other places, then this may not be a valid concern though. sorry for the late answer, please yes dm it to me anyway i think i broke lighthous ```Jun 21 13:33:08.433 WARN Chain failed! Syncing to its head won't be retried for at least the next 30 seconds, id: 16953498069082577172, from: 22811, to: 22942, end_root: 0x0bf7…b61e, current_target: 22813, batches: 8, peers: 10, validated_batches: 0, state: Syncing, service: sync``` not sure what this means but it stopped sending newPayload/Fcu is it because initial sync is unsafe? interesting, can you send me the debug logs? where can i find them 😅 ? `$datadir/beacon/logs/beacon.log` it is over 100 megabyte... will a cut version suffice? yeah should be okay, last one hour or so last 10000 lines which is past 3 hours thanks, will get back to you in a bit A quick question about this - https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/988616072842330132 (the execution client overwriting the jwt secret on each startup): Does this effectively mean that if an operator wishes to run the execution client and consensus client on separate physical machines, there needs to be an out of band synchronization on this file? Or is there a method to lock the file (simple ro *nix permissions?) and only distribute it once between machines? Hello I am from the erigon team, and just got told that Prysm supports Sepolia with a TTD of `100000000000000000000000` and an empty blockhash for TBH and was wondering if other CL clients will adopt the same number for now or not? <dannyryan> Any number exceedingly high should work as a config param currently. This just ensures it won't be hit until a precise number is decided (to be discussed on Friday acd) There is a number which is roughly that in the beacon chain config for sepolia so all clients are likely using the same number. You'll get warnings if the TTD doesn't match up between EL and CL. "roughly that" as in, I haven't tried counting the zeros. Are ELs planning on releasing updated binaries before the Sepolia TTD? Since Sepolia is mostly only run by us, we don't plan to for the fake TTD, only for the real TTD (most likely) Teku has a release out with sepolia support included now, but it doesn't have the final TTD (because it hasn't been set). We'll need to use an override for the final TTD initially as it will likely need to be applied faster than we'd want to get a release out.

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
<@301186049323958275> I'm not working on the merge directly, so <#892088344438255616> is read-only for me. In regards to 

https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/988633836193742888

I think less than 256 bits would generally be better for proving time:

As an analogy, in a 64 bit architecture, the word size is 64 bits, so if you have a datatype which requires more than 64 bits to encode its information, then you'd need multiple words. Like a u65 would need 2 64 bit words. Also adding a u65 would have more complexity to it than adding a u64 or something than is less than 64 bits.

For zk proofs, we usually have a word size that is just less than 256 bits, so to encode a 256 bit number we would also need 2 words/field elements. If its not used too often, it might be okay I think, I'd need to check the exact system/usage to determine whether the blowup may be significant.

Reasons I would not go for 234 bits would be because it may reduce the security of the system as a whole, If we are using 234 bits or even less in other places, then this may not be a valid concern though.
